scope: Whole short fixture; original failed early. Not comparable model peak/performance data.

limitations: Sampled process accounting from before exec through child exit; transients between samples can be missed.
Only the supervised PID is read, not descendants or device-wide memory; the monitor's own memory is excluded.
Status and fdinfo are read sequentially, not as an atomic snapshot; opening, closing and reusing fds can race the scan.
A size: field is not verified as DMA memory. exp_name is evidence only; dma_buffer_identity_verified remains false.
Missing inode identities are counted per fd without deduplication; missing mount IDs use an unknown-mount inode namespace.
Conflicting sizes for one identity use the largest observed size and are flagged. Unreadable or malformed fdinfo is flagged.
Allocated fd sizes are not necessarily resident bytes. Private DSP heap, driver allocations, VTCM and page cache may be absent.
Host VmRSS/VmHWM and mapped HTP arena sizes must not be added to the composite; they can overlap fd-backed memory.
VmHWM is the maximum observed kernel host high-water; a process exiting between polls may hide its final high-water.
child_final_ru_maxrss_kib comes from wait4 on Linux/Android and captures the terminated child host RSS high-water; it must not be added to sampled fd sizes or the composite.
Sampling adds CPU and procfs activity; compare baseline and candidate with the same monitor and period.
SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP are forwarded to the child process group. SIGKILL of the monitor cannot be forwarded.
